title: The legacy key leaves this slice one generic criterion, its four test cases carry no booking data, the FSD success criterion is a single line and the plan gives the slice no requirement id
source: Legacy RWB-E4-046 (Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Test cases); FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.6.4.1 (AC-P8-006-01); work package line for RWB-P8-E4046-APP (acs AC2 only, reqs empty)
description: RWB-E4-046 has two criteria. AC1 'Post a settlement booking to ALS' is owned by RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG, so this story owns AC2 'Not recorded' alone, which says only 'Given the decision log cannot be written / When the action is taken / Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003'. The four legacy test cases repeat the same two rows with no booking value: no case, no treatment, no account, no amount, no interface and no business date. The FSD keeps the feature as FEAT-PAY-06 and its main success criterion AC-P8-006-01 is one line marked 'Written one epic ahead', so the module document adds nothing. The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice, which is why section 18 traces the criterion to FEAT-PAY-06 and AC-P8-006-01 and cites the four requirement rows the harness story owns instead of claiming one. The story therefore keeps AC2 unchanged and supplies its own synthetic booking data set from the values AC1 names.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-046 AC1 and AC2 as quoted; legacy test cases TC-E4-046-01 'Post a settlement booking to ALS', TC-E4-046-02 'Not recorded', TC-E4-046-03 'Access' and TC-E4-046-04 'Principle 5' with no data column; FSD P8 v3 A2.6.4.1 AC-P8-006-01 'The data and rules it needs are in place / The trigger arrives / The result is recorded with its rule version / Written one epic ahead'; the FSD 'Requirements served' table of P8 is empty.
owner_role: P8 business analyst and the FSD owner
proposed: Publish the booking data set of FEAT-PAY-06 in FSD P8 A2.6 (case, treatment, account, accepted amount, business date, ALS interface) and give the slice a requirement row in the next split-plan version; the story needs no change because it already carries the values AC1 names.

title: No contract story is allocated to this legacy key, and the outbound manifest, the event payload, the data product code and the ALS interface values are unpublished
source: Work package line for RWB-P8-E4046-APP (H carries the two platform CONs only, no RWB-P8-E4046-CON); legacy RWB-E4-046 (Endpoints: none, Data); TSD P8 v2 T5.1 and T5.3; Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 (EV-11); RWB-P2-E4046-APP section 3; Template and Rules R5.7 and R7.3
description: The plan gives this key an app story in rwb-payment, an app story in rwb-integration and an integration harness, and no contract story at all, so the H row is the two platform CONs only. The story must nonetheless publish one event and consume one activity contract. No source gives the field list of `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1` (EV-11 is named with its producer and its consumers only), the element set of the `deliverFile(manifest)` activity it calls (the manifest is declared by RWB-P2-E1007-CON with no field table), the ALS interface id, transport, layout and result codes, the `{productCode}` of the rwb-source-data data product behind `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_payment`, or the durable timer that bounds the wait for the batch. The story publishes the event from the CloudEvents envelope, the modelled fields of the legacy key and the rule vocabulary, marks every field no source gives with the placeholder, and builds the manifest and the read-back against the published documents and their fakes.
evidence: The work package line lists `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` under H and no same-service CON; legacy RWB-E4-046 'Endpoints: None. The work runs as a service or a scheduled job inside the recovery module'; TSD P8 v2 T5.3 lists TreatmentBooked as Published with no payload; TSD P8 v2 T5.1 gives INT-03 'Core bank (ALS) | Out | Booked by the officer; confirmed on the next day's load' with no interface id or layout; RWB-P2-E4046-APP precondition reads 'The ALS interface id, its transport, the message or file layout, the result codes and the retry values are interface configuration data, not code'.
owner_role: P8 solution architect, the P2 integration owner and the event catalogue owner
proposed: Allocate a service contract baseline for this key (or extend RWB-P8-E4043-CON) that publishes `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1` in BACKWARD mode, the manifest element set of `deliverFile` with the booking branch, the error envelope and the fakes; publish the ALS interface row values as reference data and the data product code in TSD P8 appendix T-A.

title: The legacy story reads v_ace_account and v_ace_payment in process while the target gives the ACE views to rwb-source-data alone
source: Legacy RWB-E4-046 (Story, Data); FSD P8 v3 change note and A2.6.3.1 (VR-P8-006-1); context pack P8 (no ACE grant) and the slide 8 note on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05; D-RCV-35 U1 and U4
description: The legacy Data table lists `v_ace_account` (DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042) and `v_ace_payment` (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054) as the read-back source of the booking, and the legacy story states that the Workbench holds no account or payment copy. In the target only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, so DP-05 applies to this service as a prohibition and not as a permission: the booked position and the settlement payment arrive on P1's data product with its freshness stamp. The story keeps the read-back, the staleness rule and MSG-P1-001 exactly and moves the read, and the difference between the legacy data table and the target grant is recorded here so that the FSD data table and the DP-05 row agree in their next versions.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-046 Data rows 'v_ace_account | account_key, account_code, account_status, contract_no, product_category_efs, total_balance and 36 more | DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042' and 'v_ace_payment | payment_code, account_key, payment_date, payment_amount, payment_channel, capital_amount and 6 more | DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054'; FSD P8 v3 A2.6.3.1 VR-P8-006-1 reads v_ace_batch_status; the context pack names the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views as read only by rwb-source-data and lists no ACE table among the P8 ownership rows.
owner_role: P1 source-data owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Keep the read-back and the freshness check on the rwb-source-data data product, retire the v_ace_account and v_ace_payment reads of this service, and correct the Data table of FSD P8 and the DP-05 row so that no service but rwb-source-data is drawn as reading the views.

title: The work package gives the contract-dependency row as None while the story consumes four REST contracts and one activity contract, and it still starts on Day 1
source: Work package line for RWB-P8-E4046-APP (C empty, Ready to start Day 1, lane L-P8-I); the consumed rows of section 12.2 and the `deliverFile` row of section 12.5; Template and Rules R5.4 and R5.7
description: The metadata row 'Contract dependencies' is None because the work package gives C as an empty array, but the step cannot run without five answers: the accepted terms (S2), the booked position and the settlement payment (P1), the outbound item and its `deliverFile` activity (P2) and the case reference (P3). Under R5.4 a class C row never blocks the build, so the two statements do not contradict each other in effect, but they do in the plan: the five rows are built against their published documents and fakes from Day 1 and the plan's C row records none of them. The story keeps the metadata row exactly as the work package gives it and records the reads in 12.2, 12.5, 12.8 and 13.
evidence: The work package line gives 'C': [] and 'Ready to start': 'Day 1' for lane L-P8-I; section 12.2 of the story lists GET /treatments/{treatmentId}, the rwb-source-data product read, GET /admin/outbound-items and the rwb-case read, and section 12.5 lists the consumed `deliverFile(manifest)` activity; Template and Rules R5.4 reads 'C | Another service's CON story. Build against the published contract and its fake. | No'.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the split-plan owner
proposed: Add the five consumed rows to the C list of this slice in the next split-plan version (RWB-S2 treatment, RWB-P1 source-data, RWB-P2 integration, RWB-P3 case) and keep the Day-1 rule of R5.7 unchanged; the story needs no change because it already builds against the documents and fakes.

title: The legacy key tracks the booking in outbound_item, a table this service owns in the monolith and rwb-integration owns in the target
source: Legacy RWB-E4-046 (Story, Data: outbound_item, DF-OPS-168 to DF-OPS-177); context pack P8 ownership rows (one table, proceeds); RWB-P2-E4046-APP section 12.7; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01
description: The legacy story says the item is 'tracked in outbound_item' and lists `outbound_item` with DF-OPS-168 to DF-OPS-177 among the tables of the module. In the target `outbound_item` is P2 rwb-integration's table, and the Ownership Map gives this service exactly one table, `proceeds`, which this step does not write. The consequence is that rwb-payment holds no row of its own for a booking: the item, its attempts and its state are read by reference on P2's contract, the confirmation is the local decision record, and the booking reference travels on `TreatmentBooked`. The story states that split in sections 1, 8, 11 and 12.7 and adds no booking table, so the legacy data table and the ownership rows do not agree until this row is settled.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-046 'It writes nothing to ALS directly and holds no account or payment copy' with the Data row 'outbound_item | id, interface_id, idempotency_key, payload_ref, case_ids, attempt_count and 4 more | DF-OPS-168 to DF-OPS-177'; the context pack lists one P8 table, `proceeds`; RWB-P2-E4046-APP section 12.7 lists `outbound_item` in `rwb_integration` as P2's.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the P2 integration owner
proposed: Record in the next LDM version that the booking item is `outbound_item` in `rwb_integration` and that `rwb_payment` holds no booking row, and keep the item reference on `TreatmentBooked` as the booking reference the case records.

title: No source says which service raises the booking call after the accepted treatment, and the settlement path has no rejection rule row of its own
source: Legacy RWB-E4-046 AC1 ('When the case owner posts the booking'); FSD P8 v3 A2.6.2 and A2.6.3.3; RWB-P2-E4046-APP section 12.5 (the booking step may run in rwb-treatment's stage or in rwb-payment); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-SET-10, R-SET-13, R-RES-22, R-RES-23)
description: Two things are open in the booking chain. First, the trigger: R-SET-10 routes a signed settlement to operations and raises the payment instruction, the legacy criterion says the case owner posts the booking, the FSD says the step runs unattended, and P2's story allows the outbound call to come from the settlement step of TreatmentWorkflow on queue rwb-treatment or from the booking step of rwb-payment. The split plan gives the posting to rwb-payment and this story builds the booking step there, event-started by TreatmentApproved. Second, the rejection: R-RES-23 is the restructure row and no settlement row covers a booking rejected by ALS, so the rejection has no state, no message and no owner of its own in the settlement route set; the story follows the exception queue and the officer queue of P2's item and leaves the case with operations.
evidence: R-SET-10 'OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_SET | CUSTOMER_SIGNED | signed = Y | Route the case to operations and raise the payment instruction | WITH_OPS_SETTLEMENT'; R-SET-13 'WITH_OPS_SETTLEMENT | SETTLEMENT_BOOKED | agreement signed and terms booked in ALS | Set the payment due date and wait for the money'; R-RES-23 is in the restructure route set only; RWB-P2-E4046-APP section 12.5 reads 'the settlement step of `TreatmentWorkflow` on `rwb-treatment` ... or the booking step of rwb-payment where the posting runs there'.
owner_role: P8 business analyst and the Settlement route set owner
proposed: Fix the booking actor in the settlement route set (rwb-payment's booking step after TreatmentApproved), and add the settlement counterpart of R-RES-23 with its state, its message and its owner role so that a rejected booking of a settlement has a row to move by.
